entries.summary: <p>Every single Nazareth opponent this season has been ranked in the Super 25 at some point. There are highly-regarded football teams in the area that haven’t faced five ranked teams in the last two seasons combined.</p><p>Strength of schedule is wildly overlooked in many high school football polls and rankings, where remaining undefeated appears more important than playing high-quality teams.</p><p>The Roadrunners have lost to No. 7 IC Catholic, No. 2 Mount Carmel and No. 9 Montini. They have defeated No. 22 Providence and York, which started the season in the Super 25 but is now unranked.</p><p>Providence’s <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/high-school-football/2026/09/14/tyler-plantz-providence-football-fired" >head-coaching drama</a> received much of the spotlight on Friday, but Nazareth’s <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/high-school-football/2026/09/18/providence-football-tyler-plantz-nazareth" >17-10 win </a>was a hard-nosed showcase victory for the team that should be considered the favorite to win Class 6A.</p><p>A large part of the Roadrunners’ early-season struggles came from injuries. A few of those highly-recruited, college-bound players are still out. But their replacements are improving.</p><p>“We are really young,” Nazareth coach Tim Racki said. “Losing three, initially four, key players to start the season will rattle a team. You have to play a lot of guys that wouldn’t play as much. Those guys are growing up now. You get the most growth through difficulty. And we have certainly gone through a lot of difficulty the last three weeks.”</p><p>Racki’s Roadrunners started the season 0-4 in 2023 and went on to win the Class 5A state championship. In 2022, Nazareth was 2-4 after six weeks and went on to win 5A.</p><p>“Coach tells us that story about coming back from 0-4,” Roadrunners running back Chris Calhoun said. “And we have all been through this before. We just try to get better every game.”</p><h3>East St. Louis to Class 7A</h3><p>One reason Nazareth is now the favorite to win Class 6A is that East St. Louis is no longer in the way.</p><p>Earlier this week, the Illinois High School Association approved East St. Louis’s petition to move up to Class 7A. entries.title: Bears trail Vikings 6-3 at halftime
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> aren’t in Charlotte anymore.</p><p>One week after they scored 59 points in a season-opening win against the Panthers, the Bears managed just one field goal in the first half and trail the Vikings 6-3 at halftime.</p><p>The Bears’ offense was as sloppy as the weather in the first half. On their penultimate drive of the half, they completed three-straight offensive penalties — a false start, delay of game and intentional grounding — and four over five plays. They backpedaled from the Vikings’ 30 to the Vikings’ 49. Moving back out of field goal range, the Bears were forced to punt.</p><p>Williams threw his first interception of the season in the first quarter and finished the half 9-for-14 for 60 yards and a 43.7 passer rating. His <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/09/20/bears-vikings-caleb-williams-watch-wild-scramble-sunday" target="_blank" >circus scramble</a> set up the Bears’ only points of the half, a 50-yard Cairo Santos field goal in the first quarter. The blitz-happy Vikings sacked him once — on the final play of the half. </p><p>The Vikings made kicks of 35 and 49 yards to get to six points. Thirty of quarterback Carson Wentz's 70 passing yards came on one first-quarter throw to Justin Jefferson.<br></p>

entries.summary: <p>Mississippi moved into the top five with its win over LSU, the Tigers stayed in the top 10, and Florida and Mississippi State cracked the rankings to give the Southeastern Conference 10 teams in The Associated Press Top 25 college football poll released Sunday.</p><p>The Rebels, who held off Lane Kiffin and LSU 32-24 on Saturday night, jumped over the Tigers and three other teams to land at No. 4 for their first top-five ranking since they were No. 3 in the final poll last season. LSU slipped three spots to No. 10.</p><p>Texas was No. 1 for the second straight week and followed by Georgia, Notre Dame, Ole Miss and Indiana. Miami, Ohio State, Alabama, BYU and LSU completed the top 10.</p><p>The Longhorns followed up their win over Ohio State with a solid 30-6 victory over UTSA and topped the ballots of 58 of the 69 media members on the Top 25 voting panel. Indiana got four first-place votes, Georgia and Ole Miss three apiece and Miami one.</p><p>Louisville was the biggest gainer, rising seven spots to No. 16 after its 41-31 victory over SMU, which dropped six rungs to No. 22. Texas A&M took the biggest fall, going from No. 9 to No. 23 after its 31-21 home loss to unranked Kentucky.</p><p>This week's Top 25 marked the seventh time in the poll's history the SEC has had at least 10 teams ranked in a regular-season poll. The SEC had a record 11 ranked teams in back-to-back polls last September.</p><h3>In and out</h3><p>No. 21 Florida made its season debut in the rankings following a 44-39 road win over Auburn. The Gators are 3-0 for the first time since 2019 under first-year coach Jon Sumrall and in the Top 25 for the first time since Sept. 2, 2025.</p><p>No. 24 Mississippi State is in the Top 25 for the first time since 2022, when its coach was Mike Leach. That team was No. 20 in the final poll. entries.title: Second person charged with murder after man shoved from moving Red Line train
entries.summary: <p>A second person has been charged with murder in the death of 29-year-old Kyle Bickham, who was shoved from a moving CTA Red Line train earlier this month.</p><p>Katlar Parchman, 19, faces one count of first-degree murder, two additional murder counts, one count of aggravated battery of a transit employee and one count of mob action, according to Chicago police. She's the second person to be detained after a 15-year-old girl was charged last week.</p><p>Parchman of West Garfield Park was arrested Wednesday in the 200 block of North Keeler Avenue after investigators identified her as one of the people who allegedly pushed Bickham from a moving train Sept. 7 near the 69th Street station, police said. Parchman was ordered detained until trial during her first court appearance on Saturday.</p><p>On the day he was killed, a fight broke out on the train between Bickham and Parchman, the teen-aged girl and two males who haven't been charged, according to a statement from Cook County prosecutors. Police originally reported that three people attacked Bickham.</p><p>Bickham and the teen girl started arguing, and at one point, Bickham allegedly spit at the girl and hit Parchman, according to CTA surveillance footage reviewed by prosecutors. Soon after, all four attackers started repeatedly punching Bickham. One of the uncharged males choked him, while the other uncharged male pulled the emergency lever for one of the train's sliding doors as it was moving.</p><p>The 15-year-old girl grabbed Bickham by his head and shoulders and, with the help of one of the uncharged males, threw him out of the moving train, according to prosecutors. Bickham was hit by a train traveling in the other direction.</p><p>Witnesses allegedly heard Parchman say, "He shouldn't have bothered us."</p><p>Police were able to identify Parchman because she used her Ventra card to enter the 95th Street Red Line station the day Bickham was killed, according to prosecutors. After she was arrested and her phone was searched, investigators found she had allegedly looked up “good places to lay low” and “who are the police looking for."</p><p>Cook County medical examiner’s office determined Bickham died of multiple injuries from the train hitting him and ruled his death a homicide.</p><p>A 15-year-old girl was <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/09/13/15-year-old-girl-charged-murder-man-shoved-cta-red-line-train" target="_blank" >previously charged</a> with murder, mob action and felony assault of a transit employee in connection with Bickham’s death. She was also ordered detained.</p>

entries.title: With uncertainty at QB for Bears, offensive line concerns crop up, as well
entries.summary: <p>Whether it’s starter <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/09/11/as-engineer-and-artist-blend-styles-bears-ben-johnson-gets-goosebumps-about-future-with-caleb-williams" target="_blank" ><b>Caleb Williams</b></a> playing at limited capacity or backup <b>Tyson Bagent</b> filling in for him, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >the Bears</a>’ quarterback will be behind a wavering offensive line.</p><p>In the team’s 9-3 loss Sunday to the Vikings, center <b>Garrett Bradbury</b> was flagged for two holding penalties and two false starts in the first half alone, though one of the holds was negated by an offsetting penalty. And at left tackle, a position that has been an ongoing frustration for coach <b>Ben Johnson</b>, <b>Braxton Jones</b> is now in a rotation with swing tackle <b>Theo Benedet</b>.</p><p>Bradbury was part of a brutal sequence late in the second quarter, during which the Bears squandered first-and-10 at the Vikings’ 30-yard line and ended up punting.</p><p>Tight end <b>Sam Roush</b> was penalized for an illegal shift, Bradbury was called for holding and Williams drew a flag for intentional grounding to take the Bears back to second-and-35 from their own 45.</p><p>Then, with the Bears still trying to salvage a field goal on third-and-24, Bradbury was whistled again for a false start.</p><p>‘‘The penalties are inexcusable,’’ he said. ‘‘We’ll be better, and I’ll be better.’’</p><p>Johnson reluctantly named Jones his starter going into the season, just as he did last season, and once again doesn’t feel great about it. He benched him for Benedet in Week 4 last season.</p><p>The Bears were forced to pivot at center and left tackle after former center <b>Drew Dalman</b> retired and left tackle <b>Ozzy Trapilo</b> suffered a major knee injury in the playoffs last season.</p><p>There’s optimism for Trapilo, given that he completed his first full practice Friday, but he was inactive Sunday. At center, Plan A is for Bradbury to be the starter all season as the team gives second-round pick <b>Logan Jones</b> what essentially amounts to a redshirt year to learn the offense.</p><p>Johnson said that the left-tackle rotation was planned and that Bradbury is ‘‘doing a great job.’’</p><h3><b>Defense looks better</b></h3><p>It certainly helped that Soldier Field was a rainy mess and that the Vikings started journeyman quarterback <b>Carson Wentz</b>, but the Bears’ defense played much better than it did in allowing 37 points to the Panthers last week.</p><p>Wentz completed 11 of 20 passes for 143 yards and a 77.7 passer rating, and wide receiver <b>Justin Jefferson</b> finished with only three catches for 55 yards. Running back <b>Aaron Jones</b>, however, hit the Bears with 105 yards on 23 carries.</p><p>‘‘Still got a lot to clean up, but it definitely is a kick-start,’’ cornerback <b>Malik Muhammad</b> said.</p><h3><b>Injury concern</b></h3><p>For the second consecutive week, cornerback <b>Tyrique Stevenson</b> was in and out with injuries. He left with a hamstring issue, and the Bears are awaiting additional testing.</p>

entries.title: Caleb Williams hurt? Bears offense a disaster? And you thought this season was going to be easier
entries.summary: <p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/09/20/bears-vikings-caleb-williams-hurt-on-non-contact-play-nfl" target="_blank" >Caleb Williams went down</a> as if a bolt of lightning had struck him in the back of his powerful right leg.</p><p>The earth shuddered. Spirits plummeted. Angels wept.</p><p>Throughout Beardom, men and women who haven’t sprinted since the Clinton administration leaned forward in their La-Z-Boys, shook their fists at their TV screens and cursed the football gods.</p><p>No Williams? No shot at a <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> season to remember.</p><p>But let’s not kid ourselves — even with Williams, the Bears were so preposterously terrible on offense in a 9-3 loss to the Vikings that many of the warm-and-fuzzy feelings after <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/09/18/bears-offense-left-much-to-be-unpacked-in-59-point-explosion-starting-with-te-colston-loveland" target="_blank" >a season-opening 59-point eruption</a> would’ve been long gone heading into Week 3.</p><p>Had backup Tyson Bagent completed a last-ditch touchdown drive for the win instead of seeing it peter out with a sack from the 12-yard line, we’d still be asking if this Bears team is capable of blocking a dynamic defensive front.</p><p>Even if Williams had dusted himself off and finished things after hurting his right hamstring midway through the fourth quarter, we’d still be wondering if it’s going to be another season of the same old inconsistent passing attack and the same old need for crazy comebacks all over again.</p><p>Instead, Williams’ availability going forward is to be determined — just typing those words is chilling — and the 1-1 Bears are already back in the business of losing division games.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Caleb Williams walked through the locker room carrying his duffle bag, seemed upbeat, said hello to people and said, "All good," as he left.<br><br>I don't interpret "all good" as no problem, just that he has a positive attitude.<br><br>Ben Johnson said they'll know more Monday, meaning MRI.</p>— Jason Lieser (@JasonLieser) <a href="https://x.com/JasonLieser/status/2101795788732994041?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">September 20, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>One week later, eight fewer touchdowns than they scored against the Panthers. In what world should that be possible?</p><p>“That’s the NFL, you know what I mean?” wide receiver Rome Odunze said. “One week, you might score 59. The next week, you might score three. That’s how it goes.”</p><p>Yeah, that’s not supposed to be how it goes.</p><p>“Sometimes you’re in a rut, and sometimes you can’t be stopped,” he said. “We like to err on the side of can’t be stopped.”</p><p>Fans at Soldier Field like to err on the side of not getting rain dumped on them for three-plus hours, but they didn’t let a little imperfect late-summer weather stop them from doing their thing. Alas, a wickedly aggressive Vikings defense and — if you believe Bears coach Ben Johnson — the conditions conspired to turn an offense Johnson wants to be unstoppable into a frightened turtle.</p><p>“The weather was a major factor in this game,” Johnson said. “It was a big story of this game.”</p><p>Quick show of hands: Is anyone out there feeling particularly confident in the Bears’ chances to repeat atop the NFC North for the first time since 2005 and 2006?</p><p>Sure, they won the division a year ago despite a 2-4 record against the Vikings, Lions and Packers. But the Bears now are 9-28 in the division since 2019. They’re also 0-5 against Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell at Soldier Field.</p><p>That’s not how you “take the North,” especially when your franchise QB is rolling in the wet grass in agony.</p><h3><b>MAKING THE GRADE</b></h3><p><b>QUARTERBACK — C-MINUS</b></p><p>Williams went down inside the 10-yard line in the fourth quarter, a gut punch on a drive that ended up producing — talk about salt in the wound — no points. Before that, Williams’ best moments were jukes and spin moves on desperate scrambles that didn’t really amount to anything important. It’s hard to dock him too much for an essentially nonexistent passing attack considering how little time he had to operate, but it’s not like he was overly sharp when he did get a pass off. Bagent came in and led a promising final drive but, when he needed it, had no magic up his sleeve.</p><p><b>OFFENSIVE LINE — F</b></p><p>From center Garrett Bradbury’s cavalcade of first-half penalties to a unit-wide inability to create running lanes or protect their QB, the Bears utterly failed this test up front. Had the game gone on any longer, there’s little doubt the Vikings would’ve stolen the Bears’ lunch money and stuffed them in a locker. This was a bitter pill to swallow and a big step back.</p><p><b>RUNNING BACKS — D</b></p><p>Kyle Monangai ran hard, averaging 4.7 yards per carry, and D’Andre Swift had a beautiful 32-yard catch-and-run in the fourth quarter that looked like it might set up the Bears for a go-ahead touchdown. But Swift’s third-quarter fumble on first-and-goal from the 1 was a devastating mistake; as bad as the offense was, maybe the Bears are 2-0 if he hangs on to the ball there. The backs also had a rough day in pass protection.</p><p><b>WIDEOUTS AND TIGHT ENDS — F</b></p><p>Pass catchers? What pass catchers? Odunze couldn’t squeeze a third-down slant that would’ve moved the chains. Luther Burden didn’t show up until very late. The tight ends were no-shows, other than when it came to some glaring errors. Was there any type of mistake — penalties, missed blocks, a dropped potential touchdown pass — rookie Sam Roush didn’t make? (Hint: No, there was not.)</p><p><b>DEFENSE — B</b></p><p>You hold the other guys to nine points, you deserve an overall tip of the helmet even though the Bears gave up 100-plus on the ground to run-of-the-mill Aaron Jones and didn’t create any turnovers or make any truly big plays on that side of the ball. Lineman James Lynch was stout against the run, for whatever it’s worth. It’s not the “D’s” fault the Bears blew an opportunity to win a division game against far-past-his-prime QB Carson Wentz.</p><p><b>SPECIAL TEAMS — F</b></p><p>Getting a 23-yard field goal try blocked when the Bears absolutely had to have a three-spot was pathetic. Guess who got beat on the play by Isaiah Rodgers, who crashed around the end to block it? Yep, Roush.</p><p><b>COACHING — D</b></p><p>Johnson’s gutsiest decision was to go for it on fourth-and-one in the red zone in the fourth quarter, the Bears down 6-3, and they converted. On the whole, though, he got his lunch handed to him by Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores.</p><h3><b>TOMORROW’S HEADLINES</b></h3><p><b>Williams’ MRI results are in: </b>Look, just breathe into a paper bag until then if you have to.</p><p><b>Colston Loveland will — OK, might — be fine: </b>Two games, one catch, three yards. He pretty much could’ve done that without leaving Idaho.</p><p><b>Good, better, best? </b>The pressure is on Johnson now to make this thing work.</p>

entries.title: Empathy for Bears QB Caleb Williams aside, Tyson Bagent couldn't ask for a better opportunity
entries.summary: <p>This was a nightmare for <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >the Bears</a>, losing starting quarterback <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/09/11/as-engineer-and-artist-blend-styles-bears-ben-johnson-gets-goosebumps-about-future-with-caleb-williams" >Caleb Williams</a> to a hamstring injury, but aside from seeing a teammate go down, it’s the moment Tyson Bagent has wanted.</p><p>He wasn’t able to rescue them from a plodding 9-3 loss to the Vikings and cushion the gut punch of losing Williams, but he has the best opportunity of his career ahead of him if Williams misses significant time.</p><p>“I feel great,” Bagent said after mentioning multiple times how upsetting it was to see Williams get hurt. “I have a good team around me, good coaching staff, so I’m ready to roll.</p><p>“I’m grateful for any rep that I ever get. I’m ready to work hard and show up on Monday ready to go.”</p><p>He meant Monday as in the next day, but Bagent will be working toward starting the Bears’ next game, a “Monday Night Football” matchup with the powerhouse Eagles on Sept. 28.</p><p>Good thing the Bears didn’t trade him for the mere prize of a mid-round draft pick last offseason.</p><p>Johnson said little about Williams’ injury. He mentioned that the team will know more Monday — presumably from an MRI to determine the severity — and that it was “a shame” to lose him. He was relieved that it wasn’t a knee injury, but that was the most upside he could muster.</p><p>A severe tear, categorized as Grade 3, could jeopardize the rest of his season. Even a relatively minor strain could cost him multiple games.</p><p>While the injury is a major obstacle to coach Ben Johnson and the Bears, it’s the ultimate chance for Bagent to prove he’s a legitimate NFL starter. The last time this door opened for him was early in 2023 as an undrafted rookie out of Division II Shepherd when the Bears’ season was already off the rails and the offense was spiraling.</p><p>As he steps into the starting role now, Bagent is fully equipped to take charge of a team that intends to contend for a championship. If he’s as good as he and the Bears think, he’ll show it.</p><p>He’s a fourth-year veteran and, like Williams, it’s his second season working with Johnson, who signed off on giving him a contract extension last season.</p><p>Bagent entered their game Sunday against the Vikings in a pressure-packed scenario midway through the fourth quarter with the Bears in the red zone and threatening to take the lead, but they settled for a 23-yard field goal that got blocked by cornerback Isaiah Rodgers.</p><p>He got one last shot at the type of heroic escape that made Williams a star and, with no timeouts, drove the Bears from their own 35-yard line to the Vikings’ 12. He got three plays with a chance to throw to the end zone:</p><p>- A throw near the goal line to Luther Burden that Rodgers believed he intercepted, though was ruled incomplete on replay review.</p><p>- A pass to tight end Colston Loveland in the center of the end zone that fell short with safety Joshua Metellus in tight coverage.</p><p>- An 11-yard loss on a sack as time ran out and Loveland couldn’t hold off Dallas Turner.</p><p>You couldn’t help but daydream about Williams finding a way to pull it off, as he did so often last season.</p><p>“Being able to have a chance at the end zone was all you can ask for,” Bagent said. “On my end, got to be better executing when we get down there.</p><p>“It got kind of hairy for me, but unacceptable on my end. Can’t take a sack on the last play of the game — got to at least give somebody a chance.”</p><p>On short notice, and in a game in which the offense was doing next to nothing anyway, Bagent finished 5-of-9 passing for 54 yards. With Williams rarely missing so much as a snap so far, it was the most Bagent played since filling in for Justin Fields for four starts in 2023.</p><p>“It’s a tough spot for an offensive lineman to come in late in the game, so I can only imagine for a quarterback,” right guard Jonah Jackson said. “But he was trotting the field. We had the game in our hands for a second. We just couldn’t capitalize.”</p><p>If the Bears proceed with Bagent as the starter when they resume practice Wednesday, it’ll do him a world of good to get the week to regroup and work with the first team leading.</p><p>Wide receiver Rome Odunze said got enough practice reps with Bagent over the last six months that it’s “not something I’m worried about,” but Williams got the overwhelming majority of those, of course.</p><p>Chemistry doesn’t come easily, and there’s a lot that needs to improve after the Bears followed their 59-point bonanza in the opener with three in a soggy loss Sunday. They desperately need to rebound from that, and they’re hoping Bagent can do it.</p>

entries.title: Packers beat Jets in OT to end six-game skid
entries.summary: <p>EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — Trey Smack kicked a 26-yard field goal in overtime and the Green Bay Packers overcame a 10-point fourth-quarter deficit and a sloppy, penalty-filled performance to snap a six-game skid with a 20-17 victory over the New York Jets on Sunday.</p><p>Jordan Love threw two touchdown passes for the Packers (1-1), who had 14 accepted penalties and appeared on their way to another ugly loss after a fourth-quarter collapse at Minnesota last week.</p><p>But it was the Jets (1-1) who couldn't hold on in the end after mostly outplaying the Packers and stifling Love and the offense for much of the game.</p><p>The Packers also overcame a scary start when wide receiver Jayden Reed and right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele were carted off the field with injuries on consecutive plays on the opening drive. Reed has a neck injury, while Bako-Bewele hurt a knee.</p><p>The Jets won the overtime coin toss and chose to get the ball, but Geno Smith was sacked on consecutive plays by Barryn Sorrell and Lukas Van Ness, and Isaiah Williams was called for a false start, making it third-and-30. Kenyon Sadiq caught a 12-yard pass, but New York was forced to punt.</p><p>Kaleb Johnson had runs of 11 and 3 yards, and then Love connected with Chris Brooks for a 15-yard gain — and Jarvis Brownlee Jr. was called for unnecessary roughness for hitting him late. After Matthew Golden's 14-yard reception put the ball at the 8, Matt LaFleur opted to go for the field goal — and Smack sent the Packers home happy.</p><p>Love finished 16 of 29 for 145 yards with TD tosses to Christian Watson and MarShawn Lloyd.</p><p>Smith was 27 of 41 for 247 yards and a touchdown pass to Garrett Wilson for the Jets, who were also sloppy in their home opener; they were called for 13 accepted penalties.</p><p>Smith threw a 5-yard touchdown pass to Wilson to give the Jets a 14-7 lead with 2:30 left in the third quarter.</p><p>The Jets' stifling defense forced a turnover early in the fourth quarter when Kingsley Enagbare forced Lloyd to fumble and Harrison Phillips recovered. It was the fourth fumble forced by the Jets, but the first they recovered.</p><p>The drive stalled, though, and New York settled for Jason Sanders' 32-yard field goal to go up 17-7 with 11:04 remaining.</p><p>Green Bay came right back when Love threw a 3-yard touchdown pass to Watson on a play-action fake — two plays after Love's TD run was negated by offsetting penalties — to make it 17-14 with 7:58 left.</p><p>After Skyy Moore returned a punt by Austin McNamara 63 yards to the Jets 19, Smack kicked a 34-yarder to tie it with 2:59 remaining.</p><p>Green Bay took a 7-0 lead with 9:35 left in the second quarter when Love threw a dump-off pass to Lloyd, who wriggled his way into the end zone for a 6-yard touchdown. It was the first NFL touchdown for Lloyd, a 2024 third-round pick who played in just one game during his first two seasons because of injuries.</p><p>The Jets responded on their next possession with a 6-yard touchdown run by Braelon Allen, tying it at 7.</p><h3>Injuries</h3><p><b>Packers:</b> G Aaron Banks injured a toe and Donovan Jennings, his replacement, hurt a hand. DT Anthony Campbell (ankle) was injured in the first half. WR Bo Melton left in the third quarter with a stinger.</p><p><b>Jets:</b> LBs Marcelino McCrary-Ball (ankle) and Kiko Mauigoa (quadriceps) and DL David Onyemata (groin) were ruled out after halftime.</p><h3>Up next</h3><h3></h3><p><b>Packers:</b> Host the Atlanta Falcons on Thursday night.</p><p><b>Jets:</b> Face the Lions in Detroit next Sunday.<br></p>
